Question: The channel resistance of an N-channel JFET shown in the <image> is 600 \( \Omega \) when the full channel thickness \( t_{ch} \) of 10 \( \mu m \) is available for conduction. The built-in voltage of the gate \( P^+ N \) junction \( (V_{bi}) \) is -1 V. When the gate-to-source voltage \( V_{GS} \) is 0 V, the channel is depleted by 1 \( \mu m \) on each side due to the built-in voltage, and hence the thickness available for conduction is only 8 \( \mu m \).
The channel resistance when \( V_{GS} \) = -3 V is ______\Omega.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure shows an N-channel JFET, with an N-type channel in the center, and P+ gate regions above and below the channel respectively, so the conductive channel thickness is equal to the total channel thickness t_ch minus the depletion layer widths on the upper and lower sides. The figure also marks Source, Drain, Gate, and V_GS, matching the structure in which two upper and lower P+N junctions clamp the N channel. Then reason: When the full channel thickness is 10 μm, the channel resistance is 600 Ω. It is known that when V_GS = 0 V, only the built-in voltage |V_bi| = 1 V causes 1 μm depletion on each side. Now V_GS = -3 V, the gate junction reverse bias increases, so the depletion layer is driven by the total voltage magnitude 1 + 3 = 4 V. The depletion width is proportional to the square root of voltage, so the depletion width on each side becomes 1 μm × sqrt(4/1) = 2 μm. The remaining conductive thickness is 10 - 2×2 = 6 μm. The channel resistance is inversely proportional to the conductive thickness, therefore R = 600 × (10/6) = 1000 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the N channel is sandwiched between two P+ gate regions, so the conducting thickness is the full 10 µm minus two equal depletion widths. From the text, at VGS = 0 the built-in junction voltage magnitude is 1 V and causes 1 µm depletion on each side. At VGS = -3 V, the reverse-bias contribution adds to the built-in magnitude, giving a total depletion-driving voltage of 1 + 3 = 4 V. Since depletion width scales as sqrt(voltage), each side depletion becomes 1 µm * sqrt(4/1) = 2 µm. Thus the remaining conducting thickness is 10 - 2(2) = 6 µm. Because R is inversely proportional to conducting thickness, R = 600 * (10/6) = 1000 Ω.

method.method_draft: First describe the image: the P+ gates are above and below the N channel, so pinch-off corresponds to each depletion layer reaching 5 µm into the 10 µm channel. From the text, the calibration point is 1 µm depletion per side at total built-in potential magnitude 1 V.
